newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.

text.p: Analysis of key elements in Wednesday's European Cup Champions' League matches:
Group A
Auxerre (France) v Glasgow Rangers (Scotland)

Auxerre need only a draw against Rangers to secure a place in the last eight after a surprise 2-1 away victory over beleaguered Ajax. Injured goalkeeper Lionel Charbonnier and Nigerian defender Taribo West will miss the game because of suspension. Bernard Diomede will not play after damaging a shoulder in the Ajax game and influential midfielder Christian Henna is also injured. International midfielder Sabri Lamouchi and striker Antone Sibierksi have recovered from injuries and are back in the squad.

Rangers are out of the hunt for a quarter-final place but will have taken heart from their opening Champions' League victory over Grasshopper Zurich two weeks ago. They are still without Paul Gascoigne who is serving the third game of a four- match ban for kicking Ajax's Winston Bogarde last month. Also missing will be Jorg Albertz and Joachin Bjorklund who picked up injuries in Sunday's league win over Aberdeen.
Grasshopper (Switzerland) vs Ajax Amsterdam (Netherlands)

Grasshopper are injury free but will be without striker Kubilay Turkyilmaz and defender Brent Haas as both picked up second yellow cards in Glasgow two weeks ago. Romanian striker Viorel Moldovan, the Swiss league's leading scorer with 17 goals, and big midfielder Murat Yakin, scorer of the goal in the 1-0 victory over Ajax, will fill the boots of the Swiss internationals. Moldovan and Yakin spent the Rangers match on the bench because of yellow cards.

Injury stricken Ajax Amsterdam must chase a victory in Zurich to qualify for the last eight. A draw could be good enough but only in the unlikely event of Auxerre losing at home to Rangers. Despite struggling in sixth place some 13 points adrift of leaders PSV Eindhoven in the domestic league, Ajax should be lifted by the fact that they have not lost an away game in European competition for three seasons. Coach Louis van Gaal may recall international defenders Frank de Boer and Danny Blind. De Boer broke down in training before the last game, a 2-1 defeat at home to Auxerre. Group B
Atletico Madrid (Spain) vs Widzew Lodz (Poland)

Atletico, already assured of a place in the quarter-finals with 10 points, have shot back into contention in the Spanish league with five wins and a draw in six games. The winning streak coincides with the return from injury of influential Spanish international midfielder Jose Luis Caminero. Atletico hope to have Juan Eduardo Esnaider fully fit after the Argentine pulled a muscle against Racing. The only other injured player is fellow striker Leonardo Biagini. Roberto Solozabal is suspended and will be replaced by defender Juan Lopez.

Widzew, joint leaders of the Polish first division, have no chance of going through to the next round. Coach Franciszek Smuda has a full squad to choose from but said his players were "bushed" after an exhausting autumn season.
Borussia Dortmund (Germany) vs Steaua Bucharest (Romania)

Borussia are assured of a place in the quarter-finals but coach Otmar Hitzfield faces some tricky decisions. He is considering playing libero Matthias Sammer, criticised for giving in to his attacking instinct too often, in midfield because of injuries to playmaker Andreas Moeller and attacking midfielders Lars Ricken. Ricken tore ankle ligaments in Friday's 1-1 home draw against Hamburg and Moeller has a bruised calf. Defender Stefan Reuter was being treated on Monday for a thigh strain but is expected to play. Long-term absentees defenders Julio Cesar and Wolfgang Feiersinger and defensive midfielder Steffen Freund will remain on the bench.
Steaua, with only pride to play for, will be without two key players. Defender Daniel Prodan and striker Marius Lacatus are both suspended.
Group C
Rapid Vienna (Austria) v Manchester United (England)

United defender Gary Pallister is back after five weeks following a knee operation. He came through Saturday's 3-1 victory against Leicester unscathed and is expected to start a match from which United must take at least a point. The English champions, goalless in their last two European matches, will need to find more firepower up front if they are to join group winners Juventus in the last eight.

Vienna, bottom of the group, are waiting to see if Rene Wagner has recovered from flu before naming their side. If he fails to recover, Christian Stumpf will step in. Polish defender Andrzej Lesiak is suspended. The Austrians have entered their winter break and Rapid have not played competitively for the past fortnight.
Juventus (Italy) v Fenerbahce (Turkey)

"We will beat Juventus and Rapid Vienna will beat Manchester United," a confident Fenerbahce chairman Ali Sen said. The Turks go into the match boosted by two consecutive European victories over United and Rapid, knowing they must achieve as much or more than United do in Vienna. They are at full strength and will rely heavily on Bulgarian Emil Kostadinov and Nigerian Augustine "Jay Jay" Ococha.

Juventus, the newly-crowned world club champions, can relax in the knowledge they have secured a quarter-final slot but have nevertheless vowed to exit the group stage on a winning note. Coach Marcello Lippi may opt to rest French midfielder Zinedine Zidane, Croat striker Alen Boksic and playmaker Alessandro Del Piero. French midfielder Didier Deschamps is out injured as are long term absentees Antonio Conte and Gianluca Pessotto.
Group D
IFK Gothenburg (Sweden) v Porto (Portugal)

Group leaders Porto seek their fifth European win in six games but will be more concerned not to pick up yellow cards. Ten players are just one caution away from suspension. Captain Jorge Costa, head-butted by Milan's George Weah at the end of their match a fortnight ago, is still nursing a broken nose and misses the match. The Portuguese champions warmed up with a 4-2 league win over Leca at the weekend.
Gothenburg prop up the group and have little to play for but pride. Niclas Alexandersson is suspended after handling the ball in his own box in their last European match.
AC Milan (Italy) v Rosenborg (Norway)

Both teams can still qualify at the other's expense, although Milan, with home advantage and needing just a point, must be favourites. Arrigo Sacchi returns as coach after his suprise resignation from the job as Italian national coach. He has selection headaches: striker George Weah and midfielders Marcel Desailly and Stefano Eranio are suspended. Dutch midfielder Edgar Davis will be watching from the stands (hand injury) and Christian Panucci may join him (muscular problem). Milan have lost seven out of 22 league and cup games this season.

Rosenborg go into the match boosted by their win over neighbours Gothenburg a fortnight ago but are likely to be without striker Steffen Iversen who is switching allegiance to English side Tottenham. Jahn Ivar Jakobsen is suspended. The Norwegians must win to qualify and have promised an attacking approach.
